data_quality_and_counter_hypotheses: The apparent XRP spot cross-venue premium is asynchronous and partly USD/USDT basis; it is not executable arbitrage evidence.
Bid-heavy top-of-book sizes are single-level observations and cannot establish full-depth support.
The price decline may reflect broad risk-off and leverage deleveraging, but XRP-specific supply and venue effects remain untested.
Negative funding and long liquidations suggest long-side pressure, while OI direction differs across aggregators; forced long closure versus new short buildup remains unresolved.
Negative options skew coexists with call-heavy December open interest; hedging, tenor and expiry structure are competing explanations.
XRPL stablecoin supply contraction coexists with higher weekly DEX volume; the latter may reflect turnover rather than net capital.
RLUSD chain-allocation disagreement may reflect timing, bridge movement or token-mapping differences; no transfer path was verified.
ETF flow signs differ because of fund coverage, units and provisional issuer data; no common cash-flow series is established.
Global fund flows are broad macro context, not XRP-specific demand.
